title: Student-built AI flags listless and feverish lion-head geese; survival at a Shantou cooperative may have risen 30%
summary: An AI camera program built by Shenzhen University students with Tencent engineers alerts a Shantou goose cooperative to sick geese, and Xinhua reports that survival rose 30 percent.
account: In 2018 an avian influenza outbreak left five of thousands of geese alive in Houxi Village, Chenghai District, Shantou. In 2022 goose farmer Jin Shutao invited 16 students from the Shenzhen University-Tencent Cloud artificial intelligence Bachelor of Engineering program to his lion-head goose cooperative in the village. They worked in a 500 m² space holding over 4,000 geese. They used existing farm cameras and manually labeled 6,000 images of 300,000 geese. With Tencent engineers they improved recognition in crowded scenes and the tracking of how long each goose stays still. The resulting AI program identifies sick geese by measuring that stillness, supplemented by detecting feverish goslings. Xinhua reported on the program on 13 October 2023, and CGTN syndicated the report the next day. Xinhua reports that the program now gives real-time alerts for “listless geese” and “feverish geese” and displays trends in temperature, humidity and PM2.5. It states that this has helped the farm increase survival of lion-head geese by 30 percent. It quotes the student Wang Yifeng and Shen Linlin of Shenzhen University's visual research institute. The article recalls the 2018 outbreak. The 30% figure is undated, and the article gives no method behind it. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the event. On 7 September 2024 Shenzhen University and Tencent Cloud authors, including Shen Linlin, published a paper in Scientific Data. It describes six cameras on a goose farm in Chenghai District and video recorded in July and November 2022. The paper reports no figure on goose survival.
purpose: Identify sick geese from camera footage by how long they stay still (and fever in goslings) and alert breeders in real time.

fields.account: In 2018 an avian influenza outbreak left five of thousands of geese alive in Houxi Village, Chenghai District, Shantou. In 2022 goose farmer Jin Shutao invited 16 students from the Shenzhen University-Tencent Cloud artificial intelligence Bachelor of Engineering program to his lion-head goose cooperative in the village. They worked in a 500 m² space holding over 4,000 geese. They used existing farm cameras and manually labeled 6,000 images of 300,000 geese. With Tencent engineers they improved recognition in crowded scenes and the tracking of how long each goose stays still. The resulting AI program identifies sick geese by measuring that stillness, supplemented by detecting feverish goslings. Xinhua reported on the program on 13 October 2023, and CGTN syndicated the report the next day. Xinhua reports that the program now gives real-time alerts for “listless geese” and “feverish geese” and displays trends in temperature, humidity and PM2.5. It states that this has helped the farm increase survival of lion-head geese by 30 percent. It quotes the student Wang Yifeng and Shen Linlin of Shenzhen University's visual research institute. The article recalls the 2018 outbreak. The 30% figure is undated, and the article gives no method behind it. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor lists the event. On 7 September 2024 Shenzhen University and Tencent Cloud authors, including Shen Linlin, published a paper in Scientific Data. It describes six cameras on a goose farm in Chenghai District and video recorded in July and November 2022. The paper reports no figure on goose survival.
